title: Tiered circuit-breaker hysteresis and backup-restore canary playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create an operational playbook + test harness to validate active->passive promotion via a canary backup-restore while exercising tiered circuit breakers and hysteresis rules. This ticket consolidates config patterns, synthetic tests, and rollback procedures so on-call and SREs can run scheduled drills without risking customer data integrity or violating SLOs.
scope: 1) Define tiered circuit-breaker profiles for different traffic classes (control, realtime, batch). 2) Define hysteresis and cooldown policies to avoid flap on passive promotions. 3) Implement a canary backup-restore flow that performs KV snapshot restore into a quarantined passive region and runs integrity + smoke checks. 4) Add automated tests to drill-runner and dashboards/alerts in Grafana for validation. 5) Document rollback and postmortem checklist.
out_of_scope: Full automation of cross-region DNS cutover (separate ticket), full production migration of live customers (this is a canary/validation harness only), long-term cost optimization for increased snapshot frequency.
recovery_playbook_steps: 1) Prep: reserve 'drill' dedicated capacity in passive region and tag snapshots. 2) Trigger: create consistent KV snapshot (snapshot-id) and push to canary restore cluster in isolated VPC. 3) Restore: run restore job with read-only mode first, then enable limited write with canary tenancy. 4) Smoke tests: run tokenstore reads, model KV lookup, and a small generation workload at 5-10 RPS for 15 minutes. 5) Circuit breaker exercise: gradually increase synthetic failure rate (introduce 5-10% latency injections) to validate CB opens and traffic is shed according to tiered policy. 6) Validation: run checksum compare against source snapshots and application-level invariants. 7) Rollback/teardown: demote canary, revoke access, and archive artifacts. 8) Post-drill: capture metrics, annotate SLO impacts, and file findings. Note: full step-by-step commands and playbook snippets live in Confluence link attached.
circuit_breaker_config: Profile definitions: CONTROL (admin endpoints) => open_threshold: 10% failures over 30s, cooldown: 2m, half-open probes: 1rps; REALTIME (low-latency inference) => open_threshold: 5% failures over 60s, cooldown: 5m, backoff_factor: 1.5; BATCH (embeddings/long jobs) => open_threshold: 15% over 5m, cooldown: 10m. Traffic steering rules: when REALTIME CB opens, route 25% realtime traffic to dedicated 'burst' pool, 75% to degraded model variant. When both REALTIME and BATCH open, enforce progressive shedding by percentile: shed tail requests (requests > 95th percentile token length) first, then reduce concurrency per connection. All numeric values are initial hypotheses and must be validated in staging during the canary run.
hysteresis_rules: Prevent flip-flopping by requiring a sustained healthy window before closing a breaker: close only after 3 consecutive healthy evaluation windows (window length = cooldown / 3). Implement sticky-open for client sessions for 2x cooldown to preserve connection behavior. For passive promotion, require both system-level SLO pass (no >2.0% error rate in 10m) AND data-integrity checks (checksum match) before accepting write traffic. Automatic demotion if checksum delta > 0.001% or error rate spikes above 4% for control endpoints.
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: Grafana dashboard 'DR Canary Overview' (panel ids: 12, 37, 48) showing: per-region error rates, p50/p95/p99 latency, circuit-breaker states, snapshot restore duration, KV checksum delta, and tokenstore read/write success rates. Alerts: P1 alert if p99 latency > 2x SLO or if restore job fails. Alert policy links: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/DR-canary and incident runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/DR-451237. Add SLO-sla annotation to drill runs to track impact against runtime-2.4 SLOs (target: realtime p99 < 250ms, availability >= 99.95%).
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for new CB hysteresis logic in runtime repo (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4823). 2) Integration: add canary scenario to drill-runner (repo: github.com/redwood-inference/drill-runner issue #219). 3) Staging run: execute 3 back-to-back canaries across different time windows (night/off-peak, mid-day, peak) to capture behavioral variance. 4) Validation: run checksum compare, and application-level smoke tests (sample prompts, embedding lookup). 5) Acceptance: canary must complete with checksum delta <= 0.0005% and no sustained SLO breach (>5 minutes) during the trial. 6) Post-check: generate a drill report artifact and upload to the incident dashboard.
rollback_plan: If canary restore fails integrity checks or causes SLO violation: 1) Stop routing traffic to canary and promote soft-fence on promoted region. 2) Revert traffic to primary using smart-routing fallback rules. 3) Revoke canary VPC peering and snapshot access. 4) If partial writes occurred, run targeted ledger backfill from continuous WAL stored in snapshot bucket. 5) File an incident and kick off forensic snapshot comparison job. See GitHub issue for rollback automations: github.com/redwood-inference/ops-automation/issues/78.
risks: 1) Snapshot corruption during concurrent writes leading to silent data divergence. 2) Overly aggressive hysteresis causing prolonged degraded service. 3) Canary restores exposing subtle race conditions in KV reconciliation. 4) Cost spikes from reserved capacity for prolonged drills. 5) Insufficient monitoring coverage for edge SLO regressions. Mitigations: schedule runs on low-traffic windows, use read-only first, maintain forensic snapshots, and include finance on large capacity reservations.
acceptance_criteria: A playbook doc exists with clear step-by-step commands and rollback steps
Canary restore completes in staging with checksum delta <= 0.0005%
Circuit breaker transitions observed match configured hysteresis in at least two staging runs
No SLO > 5 minute breach during any canary run
Drill artifacts and a post-run report uploaded to Confluence and linked to the ticket
